Apple today unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo at its September event, but there was no standard iPhone 18. Here's why.

The standard iPhone 18 is expected to launch in early 2027, as Apple has changed its product release schedule.

You'd normally call today's Apple event the "iPhone 18 launch."

But Apple did something today that might surprise a lot of people — it didn't announce the iPhone 18, at least not the standard model.

Apple only unveiled three new high-end iPhones: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo.

This flagship lineup marks a notable departure from Apple's usual approach, where a new standard iPhone is typically unveiled alongside its Pro counterparts. However, reports as early as May 2025 had signalled this shift.

According to multiple reports, the three new iPhones Apple announced today will be joined by three more additions in early 2027:

  • iPhone 18
  • iPhone 18e
  • iPhone Air 2

So the standard iPhone 18 hasn't been cancelled — it's just arriving later than usual.

Why the change?

One explanation is that Apple wants to expand the iPhone lineup to its broadest range ever with new designs like the foldable-screened Duo, without cramming too many products into a single autumn event. Splitting the main iPhone launches between autumn and spring cycles may therefore make more sense.

Another possible reason is that Apple is anticipating the current memory shortage and knows that rolling out the standard iPhone 18, Pro models, and the Duo simultaneously would make it difficult to meet market demand.

Either way, the iPhone 18 will arrive eventually — just not until early 2027.

What are your thoughts on Apple's strategy of phasing the iPhone 18 lineup releases? Share them with us in the comments.
